instruction_template: Place in a heavy pan, cover with a tight-fitting lid, and cook on low heat for {time} min. Rotate occasionally for uniform heat distribution.
flavor_note: Maillard crust will form mostly on the contact side rather than top surface.

instruction_template: Heat a dry or lightly greased pan over medium-low heat. Cook for {time} min, turning frequently until tender and caramelized.
flavor_note: Direct conductive heat concentrates caramelization and sugar breakdown similarly to roasting.

instruction_template: Transfer to a bowl and mash vigorously with a fork or back of a spatula for 3-4 minutes until homogenous and smooth.
flavor_note: Aromatic volatile extraction is unaffected; rustic texture with slightly coarser mouthfeel.

instruction_template: Heat 1.5 cm of cooking oil in your pan over medium heat. Fry {time} min on each side until crisp and golden brown.
flavor_note: Retains same crispy lipid-bound flavor compound dissolution; requires halfway flip.

instruction_template: Bring to a rolling boil in your pot with extra 100ml water, cover tightly with lid, and simmer on gentle heat for {time} min until completely tender.
flavor_note: Slower hydrolytic extraction develops richer umami depth over extended simmering time.

instruction_template: Heat a dry frying pan on medium heat. Toast for 2 minutes per side until golden and crunchy.
flavor_note: Crisp surface contact creates identical roasted pyrazine bread aroma notes.

instruction_template: Add 2 cm of water to your pot. Place a small heat-safe bowl/plate inside to keep food elevated, cover with lid, and steam on medium heat for {time} min.
flavor_note: Steam condensation maintains water-soluble nutrients and clean aromatic integrity.

instruction_template: Cover the pot with its lid leaving a 5mm slit open at the edge. Carefully pour off hot liquid over the sink while holding the lid firmly.
Pre-heat your frying pan on maximum heat until smoking hot. Add oil and toss ingredients rapidly in small batches for {time} min.
flavor_note: Simulates wok-hei through high surface contact heat; keep portions small to prevent boiling.
